newsitem.title: GERMANY: Thyssen sees benefits in Krupp deal.
newsitem.headline: Thyssen sees benefits in Krupp deal.

text.p: Industrial group Thyssen AG saw benefits in a steel tie-up with Fried. Krupp AG Krupp-Hoesch, although it planned to advise shareholders to hold out if Krupp resumed its hostile takeover bid, a German daily said on Monday.

Thyssen was preparing to tell shareholders its shares have the potential to rise to a price of about 550 marks ($325), well above the current level of 390 marks and the 435 marks Krupp offered in a takeover bid last week, business daily Handelsblatt said.
After Krupp announced its offer last week, Thyssen agreed to discuss a joint steel company. If the talks fail, Krupp planned to reinstate its offer.

In that case, Thyssen would advise shareholders to resist, Handelsblatt said, citing confidential Thyssen documents. Thyssen believed a takeover would result in a concern with 20 billion marks in debt, the newspaper said.

Thyssen and its banking advisors have concluded that a cooperation agreement would result positive synergy effects and no additional debt, Handelsblatt said. "This could lead to special contributions in profit and special dividends for Thyssen shareholders," the paper said, quoting the documents.
Thyssen had also calculated the effects of a fusion with Krupp in business year 1991/92, Handelsblatt said.
